pr_body:
Calling _terms_enum on a constant_keyword field where the value has not been determined yet leads to a NullPointerException. We now guard against that here.

Closes #86187
Closes #86267

review_comments: I see TransportTermsEnumAction#dataNodeOperation uses getTerms(). Would it makes sense to not only check for null but also for TermsEnum.EMPTY now in L361 where we decide if we add the terms to shardTermsEnums?
TermsEnum.EMPTY does not need to be special-cased, as it works just as fine as a regular TermsEnum, it just won't yield any results.

I see TransportTermsEnumAction#dataNodeOperation uses getTerms(). Would it makes sense to not only check for null but also for TermsEnum.EMPTY now in L361 where we decide if we add the terms to shardTermsEnums?
TermsEnum.EMPTY does not need to be special-cased, as it works just as fine as a regular TermsEnum, it just won't yield any results.
I claim that TermsEnum.EMPTY is the better response here, as null is equivalent to what we return when _terms_enum is not supported on a given field type.
Would it then also make sense to use EMPTY in L166 (the searchAfter block?). I think it wouldn't NPE at the moment but potentially could if code changed? Maybe we can add a test for that too.
PS: I see one of the yaml tests already seems to test "searchAfter", am I right that this curently wouldn't result in an NPE since the value isn't really used on that code path?

The existing test with searchAfter was working on an index where the constant was already in place (i.e. `value != null`), so did not lead to a NPE.

I have now added [d808cd6](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/86191/commits/d808cd62973b91e5d4594ac56a1bc2856272276f) to use EMPTY consistently throughout.

It is more used to inform intent (stay closer to what Javadoc says) rather than making any difference in terms of behavior (both null and EMPTY are treated by caller as "to skip").
Null represents "not supported" while EMPTY signals "I know how to handle this, but there are no matching results).
